title: RankAlign: Vision-Language Representation Alignment via Rank Transformation
claim: Converting each modality's similarity kernel into an ordinal rank representation before permutation matching aligns unpaired embeddings, leaving the matching solver unchanged.
layout: 4 columns, left-to-right, dashed highlighted RankAlign box, parallel vision/language rows
description: A left-to-right pipeline with two parallel rows: purple for vision on top, green for language on the bottom. The first column, Input Data, shows images (a car, a bird) passing through a vision encoder, and text prompts passing through a language encoder. The second column, Embedding Space, shows clustered class dots that become class prototypes x1..xN and y1..yN. The third column is a dashed yellow box labeled RankAlign. In it, a value-based similarity kernel heatmap is turned into a rank-based ordinal kernel by an R(·) arrow, with the matrix notation written below each heatmap. The fourth column, Matching (Permutation), shows an optimization objective formula, then a bipartite link between visual class nodes and language class nodes through a blue box labeled optimal permutation. The eye goes first to the highlighted RankAlign box and the heatmaps.
caption: Visual-language alignment pipeline. The RankAlign module provides the core ordinal representation of each within-modality similarity kernel. These representations are refined using local neighbor order before permutation matching, without changing the matching space or solver.
abstract: While the Platonic Representation Hypothesis posits that vision and language models converge toward compatible latent geometries, recovering class-level correspondences between unpaired modalities without cross-modal supervision remains challenging. Existing relational matching methods compare within-modality similarity kernels directly, although the same semantic structure may be represented through different numerical parameterizations across modalities. We propose RankAlign, a rank-based normalization strategy for class-level unpaired vision-language matching. RankAlign transforms each within-modality similarity kernel into an ordinal relational representation before permutation matching, while leaving the correspondence space and matching solver unchanged. The resulting representation is invariant to strictly increasing reparameterizations of similarity values while preserving the ordinal structure used for matching. We provide exact-recovery and stability guarantees that characterize correspondence recovery under both exact and partial ordinal agreement. Experiments across diverse frozen vision and language encoders and multiple datasets demonstrate improved and more stable class-level correspondence recovery, including under label corruption and domain shift.
